hooks.text: A 1,000-foot city killer slipped right past Earth without anyone noticing.
A 600-megaton threat passed Earth, but nobody saw it coming.
Nine days after a 1,000-foot asteroid passed Earth, astronomers finally noticed.

title: The Stealth Asteroid That Missed Earth
description: In March 1989, a 1,000-foot asteroid swept past Earth completely unnoticed until astronomers spotted it nine days later.

beats.text: A 1,000-foot city killer slipped right past Earth without anyone noticing.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a near-Earth asteroid approaching Earth, 2021

beats.text: On March 31, 1989, astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas spotted a faint streak at Palomar Observatory.
beats.visual: photograph of the dome exterior at Palomar Observatory in California, 2012

beats.text: When they calculated its orbit, the data revealed something terrifying.
beats.visual: orbital diagram of Apollo-group near-Earth asteroid system, 2020
queries: near Earth asteroid orbit diagram NASA

beats.text: Nine days earlier, in late March 1989, this massive rock had swept past our planet.
beats.visual: illustration of an asteroid flying closely past Earth and Moon, 2019
queries: near Earth object pass Earth visual

beats.text: Designated 4581 [Asclepius](/æzklˈipˈiˌʌs/), it missed us by 425,000 miles, roughly twice the distance to the Moon.
beats.visual: DSCOVR spacecraft view showing the Earth and Moon together in space, 2015

beats.text: Had it struck an ocean, calculations showed it would unleash the power of a 600-megaton atomic explosion.
beats.visual: artist's concept of an asteroid impacting Earth's ocean, 2018

beats.text: The shock of missing this close call forced governments to establish modern planetary defense networks.
beats.visual: artist's concept of NASA's DART spacecraft impacting an asteroid, 2022

beats.text: It was a chilling reminder of how easily a massive asteroid can sneak past us.
beats.visual: OSIRIS-REx spacecraft image of boulder-strewn asteroid Bennu, 2019

better_than_last: Uses a mystery structure to build tension around an undetected asteroid before revealing its 600-megaton threat scale and looping seamlessly back to the hook.
